Character options for Hold Please

Ten ways to get the people right. Every image is the pack's own preview, so what you see is what you get. Reply with a number (or two) and I build it. The two left pictures are the real game, the two right ones are what we have now.

Reference

The options

1 Synty — POLYGON Office Pack
paid · £27.53 on sale when I checked (regular £45.89)18 charactersrigged, humanoidFBX in Unity/Unreal packages+ 500 office props

Office workers with headsets, shirts, suits and lanyards, in the chunky low-poly style the real game is clearly made in. Comes with the whole office too (cubicles, water cooler, boxes), which we could swap in as well.

Looks like the real game ●●●●●
What it takes: you buy it on syntystore.com and hand me the zip; I convert FBX → GLB, retarget sit / type / walk animations, add the orange skins, chains and headsets if you want the scam look on top. About a day.
2 Kenney — Animated Characters (Protagonists · Retro · Survivors)
free · CC0one rig · 4 skins per packFBX + PNG skinsidle · jump · run clipsbig round heads

Soft-shaded cartoon people with oversized heads — the proportions closest to the real game's among the free packs. The Protagonists pack has a moustached man in a white suit who is already a scammer. Three packs, twelve painted skins on one shared body (I checked the files: FBX, textures, three clips).

Looks like the real game ●●●●○
What it takes: half a day — convert with Blender (installed here), keep idle and run, pose sitting and typing myself, bolt the headset, chain and badge to the head and chest bones, paint the skins orange. No purchase, no login; already downloaded.
3 Quaternius — Ultimate Modular Men + Women
free · CC011 + 10 characters24 animationsglTF · FBX4 swappable parts eachfiles on a Google Drive folder

Proper "normal people" low-poly: suits, workers, casual wear, a horse-head guy. Heads and bodies mix and match, so a call floor of 16 different scammers is easy. Less cartoon than the real game, more realistic proportions.

Looks like the real game ●●●○○
What it takes: half a day — glTF loads straight in, 24 clips (idle, walk, run, actions) to pick from, I pose the rig for typing, recolour skins orange and add chains/headsets. Free, no login.
4 Quaternius — Ultimate Animated Character Pack
free · CC052 charactersanimatedFBX · OBJ · Blend (no glTF)

Fifty-two chibi characters — suits, cops, chefs, cowboys, zombies — tiny bodies, big heads, dark faces with white eyes. Funny and very "game", but a different cartoon than the real one.

Looks like the real game ●●○○○
What it takes: a day — FBX needs converting, the faces have no mouths so the webcam blinking/grinning would go; the rest as option 3.
5 Kenney — Blocky Characters
free · CC0100+ charactersseparate parts20 animation filestextured

Minecraft-style blocks with painted faces: businessmen, a cop, a bald man with glasses, moustaches, suits with red ties. Instantly readable as "a scammer in a suit", but it is a different game's look.

Looks like the real game ●●○○○
What it takes: 2–3 hours — their parts map one-to-one onto the puppet I already animate (head, body, arms, legs), so typing, blinking and the scratch all keep working.
6 KayKit — Adventurers character pack
free · CC08 charactersrigged + animated25+ accessoriesfantasy outfits

The cutest of the lot — chunky toy people with expressive faces and beards. But they are knights, mages and barbarians; I would have to strip the armour and recolour everything into polo shirts.

Looks like the real game ●●○○○
What it takes: a day, most of it undressing them. Free, no login.
7 Adobe Mixamo characters
free with an Adobe login~100 characters2,000+ animationsauto-riggeryou download, I cannot log in

Realistic-ish 3D people and the best animation library there is (sitting, typing, phone talking, all of it). The look is smoother and more "3D film" than the real game's cartoon.

Looks like the real game ●●○○○
What it takes: you pick 4–6 characters and the sit/type/walk clips on mixamo.com and give me the FBX files; a day to integrate. Mixamo's auto-rigger also makes option 9 animatable.
8 Poly Pizza — single models
free · CC-BY (credit the author)one model at a timemixed stylesfree account to download

Business Man, Worker, Retail Worker, Woman with a headset… thousands of singles by different artists. Good for one hero character; a whole call floor from singles never looks like one team.

Looks like the real game ●●○○○
What it takes: per model, an hour; attribution line in the credits.
9 Made to order with AI (Hunyuan3D on your Higgsfield credits)
~11 credits per modeltextured meshnot riggedunique

I describe exactly the scammer we want — orange egg head, moustache, polo with badge, gold chain, headset — and get a textured model back, one per character. Looks the most "ours"; moves the least: a static mesh unless we run it through Mixamo's auto-rigger (option 7).

Looks like the real game ●●●●○
What it takes: 2–3 generations to get one right (~30 credits), then rigging through Mixamo (your login) if you want them to type and walk.
10 Keep mine, restyle to the option you point at
freeimmediateeverything keeps working

The people are built in code, so I can rebuild them to any of the looks above ("like 2 but orange", "like 1 but chunkier") without downloading anything — blinking, typing, scratching, co-op and the webcam all stay.

Looks like the real game ●●●○○ (depends on the brief)
What it takes: an afternoon per iteration.
My pick: 1 if you are willing to pay — it is the same kind of asset the real game is made of. If not, 2 (Kenney Animated Characters) is the closest free match to the real proportions, with 3 (Quaternius modular) as the "more real people" alternative. 9 is the wildcard if you want them to look like our scammers and nobody else's.
